daily_thesis: The 2026-08-21 batch is about turning robot intelligence into auditable interfaces before deployment. VLA and manipulation papers expose embodiment mismatch, continual skill retention, latent-action choice, tactile world-action forecasts, and contact topology as separate variables that can change the next action. Autonomy and geometry papers do the same for scenario-conditioned evaluation, temporal-logic constraints, LiDAR degeneracy, metric registration, and sparse-view reconstruction. The shared research move is to make the evidence gate visible: what observation, contact state, map property, scenario condition, or generated process is allowed to authorize the policy.

clusters.cluster: VLA adaptation moves from single finetunes to embodiment-safe action interfaces
clusters.why: Existing robot adaptation often asks whether a single finetune raises task success on the new embodiment. This group instead exposes where adaptation can fail: self-demonstrated VLA data can overwrite old competence, skill-subspace updates can forget previous velocity mappings, latent-action design choices can hide inconsistent evaluation, tactile world-action models can miss contact hierarchy, and whole-body WAMs must split camera ego-motion from base and arm action. APRL should evaluate adaptation at the interface that changes the next action, not only at final task success.
clusters.confidence_note: Six Robot Learning papers independently target VLA finetuning, continual skills, latent actions, tactile WAMs, whole-body WAMs, or offline action modeling.
clusters.lab_action: Run equal-budget manipulation and mobile-manipulation tasks with new gripper geometry, old-skill probes, latent-action variants, tactile contact shifts, and base-arm coupling; compare next-action delta, forgetting rate, contact recovery, ego-motion error, and final success.

clusters.why: A final grasp or traversal score hides the physical state that made the behavior reusable. frontier_memory.label: Contradiction
frontier_memory.history: Recent VLA adaptation work wants broad transfer, while safety and evaluation papers require narrow evidence gates.
frontier_memory.body: The useful research tension is whether gating, shielding, and scenario conditioning improve deployment without destroying the flexibility that made VLA policies attractive.

frontier_memory.label: Missing axis
frontier_memory.history: The repo still lacks a shared benchmark that connects VLA adaptation, evidence-gated planning, contact-state prediction, and map degeneracy in one episode.
frontier_memory.body: APRL can own that missing axis by designing episodes where the same hidden evidence variable affects planning, contact, and localization decisions.

strategy_board.title: Evidence-gated mobile manipulation protocol
strategy_board.thesis: Require each VLM-TAMP subgoal, VLA action, and safety branch to cite the observation or predicate that authorizes execution.
strategy_board.one_week: Create ten tasks with hidden goal objects, misleading language priors, branch-pair safety conflicts, and small visual evidence.
strategy_board.four_week: Evaluate VLM-TAMP, VLA, and embodied-agent baselines with evidence availability, unauthorized subgoal, branch violation, and recovery labels.
strategy_board.success: Evidence gates reduce unsupported subgoals or unsafe actions while preserving at least 90% of clean-task success.
strategy_board.stop: If gates only delay execution and do not change failure or safety outcomes, narrow the protocol to observation acquisition.
strategy_board.asset: Evidence-gated task set, observation labels, branch-pair predicates, subgoal authorization traces, and recovery outcomes.

strategy_board.title: Contact-and-whole-body world-action benchmark
strategy_board.thesis: Compare tactile hierarchy, latent actions, self-demonstrated VLA adaptation, and decoupled whole-body forecasts under the same contact-rich tasks.
strategy_board.one_week: Instrument one door traversal and one dexterous grasp task with tactile, ego-motion, arm-motion, and action-chunk labels.
strategy_board.four_week: Train or evaluate equal-budget policies with self-demonstrated data, latent-action variants, tactile WAM, and decoupled whole-body WAM.
strategy_board.success: A hidden contact or ego-motion label predicts the next-action correction before terminal success changes.
strategy_board.stop: If hidden labels do not change policy ranking or recovery choice, split manipulation and locomotion tracks.
strategy_board.asset: Contact traces, tactile forecasts, ego/arm action factors, latent-action labels, and whole-body recovery logs.

strategy_board.title: Scenario-conditioned deployment confidence
strategy_board.thesis: Turn simulation-augmented evaluation, temporal logic, risk-weighted inspection, and reachability into explicit scenario coverage claims.
strategy_board.one_week: Define four scenario families: partial observability, degenerate map, dynamic obstacle, and reachability boundary.
strategy_board.four_week: Compare policy confidence from real rollouts, simulation proxies, temporal-logic monitors, and reachability audits across those families.
strategy_board.success: Scenario-conditioned confidence changes deployment decisions relative to one aggregate success estimate.
strategy_board.stop: If confidence intervals and policy rankings remain unchanged across scenario families, keep only the cheapest evaluator.
strategy_board.asset: Scenario taxonomy, monitor predicates, simulation-real pairs, reachability labels, and deployment confidence reports.
